countries.source: U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve
countries.note: Constant-maturity par yields published by the U.S. Treasury.

countries.source: Bank of Canada benchmark bond yields
countries.note: The Bank of Canada does not publish a 1-year benchmark bond. The long-term benchmark is the 30-year point.

countries.source: Bank of England nominal gilt spot curve
countries.note: Anderson–Sleath fitted nominal government spot curve. This is a spot rate, not a coupon-bond par yield.

countries.method: Par yield from the Svensson curve, annual coupon, percent
countries.note: Yields derived from the Bundesbank term structure for listed federal securities with annual coupon payments.

countries.source: Banque de France TEC 10, via comptespublics.fr
countries.note: Only the 10-year TEC is in the keyless public republication of Banque de France data. Other tenors are left blank. A free Webstat API key fills them on the weekday job.

countries.method: Monthly average gross yield to maturity, percent
countries.note: September 2026 monthly averages from Banca d'Italia table BMK0100, published 15 October 2026. The bulletin PDF could not be downloaded automatically, so this row is that verified table rather than a fresh parse. 1Y, 2Y and 7Y are not in the table.

countries.source: Japan Ministry of Finance JGB interest rates
countries.note: Daily Japanese government bond yields published by the Ministry of Finance.

countries.source: Reserve Bank of Australia statistical table F2
countries.method: Interpolated Australian government bond yield, percent per annum
countries.note: Table F2 publishes 2-, 3-, 5- and 10-year yields only.
The public ChinaBond government curve shows 3M, 6M, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, 7Y, 10Y and 30Y. There is no 2Y point on that page.

countries.source: Financial Benchmarks India G-Sec par yield curve
countries.method: Par yield, semi-annual YTM, percent per annum
countries.note: FBIL par-yield curve. The figure used is the published semi-annual YTM, not the annualized column.

compoundingNote: Yields are shown as each source publishes them. Compounding conventions differ by market and are not converted.
